scenarios.title: One elected workbench host per accepted input edge
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract, not observed game evidence: FakeModContext, CreatorWorkbenchRouter and two authenticated competing hosts; count actual callback invocations and snapshot registration identities before acquisition and after disposal. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Register a running Sandbox host and lower-priority competing host with the configurable shared binding.
Dispatch one accepted synthetic input edge and independently count the elected callback; reject non-running, stale, headless and incompatible-host paths in separate negative fixtures.
Dispose both registrations and dispatch the old binding again; measure callbacks and router registrations.
cleanup: Dispose registrations in reverse acquisition order, then the router and test context.
Compare owned input and host registrations with the captured baseline; assert no fake context leaks.
negativeTests: Give both hosts a callback recorder: a second invocation from one edge must fail the count oracle.
Retain a stale callback after unregistering its host and fail if it invokes the retired host.
Exercise wrong gamemode, loading/stopping and simulated remote admission without treating a fake participant as native multiplayer.

residualRequirements.oracle: Send a real F5 down/up pair to the receipt-bound foreground game and correlate one elected Sandbox toggle with actual visibility.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Hold or duplicate the edge, lose foreground, or target the wrong process; abort actuation or detect duplicate/wrong toggles.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release all held keys and verify the original owned process and control baseline.

residualRequirements.oracle: A genuinely connected remote participant must exercise the declared host policy when a supported live transport exists.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A fake participant or local loopback must remain classified as offline, never a real remote pass.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Disconnect only fixture-owned peers and verify session, registration and input cleanup.

residualRequirements.oracle: Observe that the correct tool opens once, identifies its owner and can be closed through accessible controls.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Have the operator identify a wrong owner or visually duplicated surface independently of a callback count.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Close fixture surfaces and confirm player control/cursor recovery.

scenarios.title: Catalog spawn, transform, duplicate and temporary visibility
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: one authenticated prop source and borrowed scene target through CreatorContentService or its testing fake; record actual factory/adapter calls, entity identity and owner-tagged roster state. Required counts specify fixture behavior only. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Browse and select the pinned source-qualified prop entry through captured workbench controls.
Spawn one owned object, apply one transform, duplicate once and temporarily hide one borrowed target; independently observe four successful fixture operations.
End the session and compare borrowed transform/visibility and foreign-owner objects with their pre-session snapshots.
cleanup: Restore borrowed edits before disposing owned objects and registrations.
Dispose the source/session/context and verify the original borrowed-state fingerprint and resource baseline.
negativeTests: Remove the source or expected catalog entry before selection and require a bounded unavailable outcome.
Return a foreign-owner duplicate recipe, a throwing factory or a partial transform failure; reject false success and release reservations.
Seed one missing restore or retained duplicate and require the restoration or owned-count oracle to fail.

residualRequirements.oracle: Production widgets in the pinned Editor must expose the intended search, list, selection, transform, visibility and duplicate controls with usable hit regions.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Render a clipped or disabled required control and fail visual/semantic assertions despite successful controller calls.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Dispose UI hosts, pooled elements and subscriptions to their measured baselines.

residualRequirements.oracle: Exercise every admitted item, prop and RobotKit type from the exact candidate inventory and inspect native identities, transforms, visibility and roster membership.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Omit an expected type or make the rendered selection disagree with the mutated native target; fail the mapped case.
residualRequirements.cleanup: End the session and confirm owned native objects disappear while borrowed/foreign objects restore.

residualRequirements.oracle: Use real keyboard and pointer dispatch to search, select and edit through production hit regions.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Invoke a controller callback without matching focused control/input evidence and refuse a native UI claim.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release device input and restore the prior focus and player-control state.

scenarios.title: Borrowed robot previews and conflict-aware restoration
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: FakeRobotSceneEditorService with a preexisting robot whose transform, personality fields/identity and brain data are independently snapshotable. The positive fixture has no external writer; conflict and disappearing-target behavior are separate negative fixtures. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Acquire one exclusive borrowed-robot edit lease.
Apply one transform, one personality preview and one brain preview, independently checking three accepted mutations against the fake robot state.
End the session and compare the non-conflicting robot snapshot with its baseline; inspect retained temporary objects and leases.
cleanup: Attempt every owned restoration even if another disposer throws, then release the edit reservation.
Dispose workbench and fake context after recording the restoration result; retain external-writer state in the separate conflict fixture.
negativeTests: Write different robot state outside the lease after preview; require Conflict, preserved outside changes and visible failure propagation instead of a false restored message.
Destroy the borrowed target or fail halfway through preview; require bounded failure and released ownership without resurrecting it.
Seed a leaked temporary personality or stale brain snapshot and fail the independent state/resource oracle.

residualRequirements.oracle: Capture the real isolated robot transform, personality identity/fields and brain state before preview and after End Session; verify temporary Unity objects are destroyed.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Inject a native external writer or disappearing target and require preservation/refusal without claiming unconditional exact restoration.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release native edit ownership; retain original conflict evidence and preserve all unrelated state.

residualRequirements.oracle: Observe that a restore conflict or incomplete restoration is described accurately to the player, with no success message hiding it.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Present a conflict behind a generic restored toast and require a recorded usability failure.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Dismiss notifications without deleting evidence and return the fixture to its approved known state.

scenarios.title: Source unregister and reentrant teardown preserve other owners
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: an authenticated source owns two spawned fake instances while a second source owns one control instance. Record exact factory disposal callbacks, catalog identities and foreign state; no fake vehicle is a native vehicle claim. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Register both sources and spawn two objects from the source that will unload plus one foreign control object.
Unregister the first source, including a reentrant callback fixture, then advance the defined fake frame barrier.
Observe exactly two owned-instance disposals and compare the control source/instance fingerprint with its baseline.
cleanup: Prune retired source entries and stale roster references, releasing every source edit and instance exactly once.
After measurements, dispose the foreign control source and context and assert no leaks.
negativeTests: Reenter unregister or End Session from the first disposal callback; fail duplicate disposal or skipped later cleanup.
Make one source disposer throw; require the remaining owned disposals to run and report the failure.
Attempt stale catalog selection after unregister; it must not spawn from the retired factory.

residualRequirements.oracle: Unload a fixture package through supported manager lifecycle and observe native character objects, catalog entries and edit leases retire once.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Keep one native object or stale entry after owner unload and fail even if the registry count is zero.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Unload only fixture-owned packages and verify unrelated content survives.

residualRequirements.oracle: Exercise a validated native vehicle factory only after such an adapter is implemented and admitted for build 2409.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A fake vehicle or empty category cannot pass vehicle creation/unload; record unavailable capability.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release every admitted vehicle object and registration, or verify refusal left no mutation.

scenarios.title: Hiding retains the session while releasing player-control ownership
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: one CreatorWorkbench, one manual robot and a stable fake session identity; record control leases, captured warning HUD and object identity. One sample covers one open/hide/reopen/end sequence. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Open, create the manual robot and record session and robot identities.
Hide once and observe retained session/content, zero workbench control leases and the captured reopen warning HUD.
Reopen once without replacing the session, then End Session; count one accepted reopen and measure final ownership.
cleanup: End rather than merely hide the session, dispose the workbench and compare the fake lifetime/UI/input baseline.
Release any test-owned source registrations and assert no context leaks.
negativeTests: Replace the session or robot on reopen and fail the identity observation.
Retain a control lease while hidden, omit the warning HUD or invoke recursive dismissal; fail the corresponding assertion.
Invoke a retired hide/reopen callback after disposal and require it to produce no new surface or session.

residualRequirements.oracle: Measure actual movement/camera input while visible, hidden and reopened; confirm hide restores controls and reopening suppresses the appropriate framework actions.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A zero lease count with blocked movement or a visible workbench with unintended gameplay input must fail.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release keys/buttons, end the owning session and verify native cursor/control restoration.

residualRequirements.oracle: Render the production hidden-session warning HUD at supported UI scales, contrast and reduced-motion settings.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Hide or clip the warning while the session remains active and fail the image/semantic oracle.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Dispose the HUD/window and verify allocator, tween and subscription baselines.

residualRequirements.oracle: Confirm a player can tell temporary edits remain active while the workbench is hidden and discover how to reopen or restore them.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Present an ambiguous or missing warning and record failure even when session retention is correct.
residualRequirements.cleanup: End the fixture session explicitly and verify the warning retires.

scenarios.title: Unavailable mutation isolation refuses global writes

The shipped Sandbox has no global persistence-isolation lease; fake ready/revoked cases are separate contract checks. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Attempt one global mutation without a valid persistence-isolation lease and record its explicit refusal.
Read the fake persistence write log and state snapshot independently of the returned status.
In separate negative fixtures cover denied acknowledgement and ready-then-revoked fake safety, keeping their scope explicitly offline.
cleanup: Release acknowledgements, safety registrations, sessions and control ownership even on refusal.
Verify the refused fixture state fingerprint and write counter are unchanged before disposing its context.
negativeTests: Supply an unavailable or revoked bridge and fail if any mutation or write is accepted.
Dismiss acknowledgement instead of confirming and require refusal with no lease acquisition.
Fabricate a successful native-global result from a fake lease and require scope rejection.

residualRequirements.oracle: On the isolated game, hash an approved synthetic save/checkpoint allowlist and observe refused unsupported global mutation with no unexpected create/delete/write.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Allow one write or an unexplained success despite the unavailable bridge and fail the refusal case.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Preserve private before/after evidence and touch only the approved QA persistence roots.

residualRequirements.oracle: A separately approved native bridge must demonstrate acknowledgement, real write isolation, mutation and revocation restoration before successful global coverage exists.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A fake lease, in-memory copy or untouched save path cannot stand in for native persistence isolation.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Revoke and restore every admitted lease; preserve failed layouts until owned process exit is confirmed.

scenarios.title: Graph Stop removes graph effects and preserves manual content
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: a branching graph with one graph-owned object, one borrowed edit, one interaction, one synthetic conversation and one audio handle beside a separately owned manual object. Inspect actual fake service records, not graph success labels. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: Start the bounded branching graph and independently count five acquired graph effect handles.
Stop through the captured production workbench control and run the defined cancellation/frame barrier.
Observe all graph handles/callbacks stopped while the manual object identity and state remain unchanged.
cleanup: Attempt all graph cleanup in reverse ownership order, restoring borrowed edits and stopping conversation/audio.
Retain manual content until after the Stop assertions, then End Session and dispose the fixture context.
negativeTests: Throw in an early disposer and require later cleanup plus explicit failure reporting.
Deliver a late conversation/audio completion or reentrant entity removal after Stop; fail resurrected handles or callbacks.
Stop before Start, exceed a graph budget or inject a graph fault; require bounded cancellation and no foreign-content loss.

residualRequirements.oracle: Observe actual spawned objects, borrowed state, interactions, conversations and audio handles cease after real UI Stop while manual content survives.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Leave one native effect active after Stop and fail despite fake runner or callback success.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Cancel every fixture effect, end its session and verify native resources and player controls restore.

residualRequirements.oracle: Capture a distinct synthetic cue on an approved device and verify bounded post-Stop silence while an unrelated control cue remains detectable.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A disconnected recorder, silent input or continuing graph cue must not produce a passing audio observation.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Stop fixture audio/capture and restore approved device settings without recording personal speech.

residualRequirements.oracle: Have the operator hear the synthetic cue and its cessation through the intended output and assess understandable Stop feedback.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A passing loopback waveform with inaudible physical output remains an unresolved device/usability case.
residualRequirements.cleanup: End playback, release device ownership and retain only approved synthetic recordings.

scenarios.title: Ten complete offline cycles preserve the same restoration baseline
scenarios.fixture: Deterministic offline contract: ten ordered samples with the same fixture shape and measured restoration baseline. Each sample opens, spawns, edits, hides, reopens, starts/stops a graph and ends its session. Expected counts are requirements, never fabricated measurements. Positive equals/count exercise counters start at zero for each sample; their expected values count only that sample's exercised actions.
actions: For each sequence 1 through 10 run exactly one complete open/spawn/edit/hide/reopen/graph/Stop/End cycle with fixed fake inputs.
Record one completed-cycle count and all post-barrier resource counts separately for every sample.
Fingerprint owned object, edit, UI, input, graph, interaction, conversation, audio, callback and synthetic persistence state before and after each cycle; retain intermediate failures.
cleanup: Apply documented synchronous/cancellation barriers before measuring; do not use repeated garbage collection or retries to hide leaks.
Dispose fixture services after all samples, assert no leaks and keep first-failure observations immutable.
negativeTests: Omit or reorder a sample, repeat a sequence number or supply only final aggregate counts; require parser or cycle-count failure.
Leak one resource only on an intermediate cycle and require that sample to fail even if later cleanup succeeds.
Change an unchanged-metric baseline between cycles and require drift failure; reject post-Stop late callbacks.

residualRequirements.oracle: Run production UI create/clear/dispose with measured canvas, allocator, tween and subscription baselines; keep the existing sixteen authoring cycles separate.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Seed a hidden canvas/subscriber leak and fail the affected cycle instead of relying on a final garbage collection.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Dispose owned Editor fixture hosts and retain diagnostic artifacts without changing the required authoring matrix.

residualRequirements.oracle: Run all ten full native Sandbox cycles against exact candidate bytes and observe independent per-cycle object, lease, input, callback and QA persistence baselines.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A fake cycle, final-only resource total or unconfirmed process exit cannot satisfy native lifecycle evidence.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release all session/fixture owners and confirm original process exit before any approved layout cleanup.

residualRequirements.oracle: Use admitted physical input/audio devices throughout repeated cycles and record device availability, foreground identity and actual control response.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: A lost/disconnected device or replayed callbacks without native input observations leaves the affected branch incomplete.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Release every held key/button, stop capture and restore approved device settings.

residualRequirements.oracle: Review sustained usability, warning visibility, focus recovery and actual audio/device quality over repeated sessions.
residualRequirements.negativeTest: Declining responsiveness or confusing recovery despite stable counters is an observed failure.
residualRequirements.cleanup: Restore QA preferences and submit attributable review with all failed and blocked subcases.
